newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan city converts sewage into electricity.
newsitem.headline: Japan city converts sewage into electricity.

text.p: Japan, tired of its huge dependency on oil, has looked high and low for a cleaner source of energy.
Now the city of Yokohama claims to have found it in the least likely of places -- sewage.
"We've succeeded in turning sludge into clean energy," an official for the Yokohama municipal government said on Wednesday.

The city's sewerage department, which purifies sewage water for the sprawling urban community near Tokyo, ends up with large quantities of a by-product composed of human, domestic, and industrial waste.
This sludge, officials say, produces "digestive gases" comprised of 65 percent methane and 35 percent carbon dioxide.
The sewerage department uses the methane to produce hydrogen, which can then serve as feed for a fuel cell.
Fuel cells generate electricity via the chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen.
"It's the world's first fuel cell using methane extracted from sewage sludge," said the Yokohama official.
The department, which has been experimenting with the technology for more than a year, has devised a system some 3.5 metres (11 feet) tall and seven metres (23 feet) wide.
The system has been been running stably over the last 30 days with a generation capacity of 200 kilowatts, enough to provide power for 100 average households, the official said.

Officials say the sludge-powered fuel cell system provides a cleaner alternative to hydrocarbon technologies, producing about one-fifteenth the nitrogen that would come from burning coal and one-sixth the nitrogen from burning oil.
